name: Hummingbird Mint
description: Hummingbird Mint (Agastache spp.) is a fragrant ornamental herb that is generally considered safe for cats. It is not listed as a toxic plant by major veterinary poison references. The plant has aromatic oils that may smell strong to cats, but these oils are not expected to cause poisoning during normal household contact. As with any plant that is not part of a cat’s diet, eating a large amount can still upset the stomach. If your cat nibbles a small amount, serious symptoms are not expected. Watch for mild vomiting or diarrhea if your cat eats more than a little. Move the plant if your cat keeps chewing it, and call a veterinarian if symptoms are more than mild or do not improve.

symptoms.name: Vomiting and Diarrhea
symptoms.notes: Eating any plant that is not part of a cat's normal diet can cause mild, self-limiting stomach upset. This is not a documented toxicosis specific to Hummingbird Mint and is expected to be transient.

symptoms.name: Drooling or Foaming at the Mouth
symptoms.notes: Hypersalivation can occur as a transient reaction to the strong taste of the plant. It is not a documented toxic effect of Hummingbird Mint.
